cve_summary: A NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in the function nfc_genl_deactivate_target() in net/nfc/netlink.c in the Linux kernel before 5.1.13 can be triggered by a malicious user-mode program that omits certain NFC attributes, leading to denial of service.
commit_message:
nfc: Ensure presence of required attributes in the deactivate_target handler

Check that the NFC_ATTR_TARGET_INDEX attributes (in addition to
NFC_ATTR_DEVICE_INDEX) are provided by the netlink client prior to
accessing them. This prevents potential unhandled NULL pointer dereference
exceptions which can be triggered by malicious user-mode programs,
if they omit one or both of these attributes.

Signed-off-by: Young Xiao <92siuyang@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
docstring:
/******************************************************************************  
 * Summary:  
 * Deactivates a target in an NFC device based on provided attributes.  
 *  
 * Parameters:  
 * skb (struct sk_buff *): Pointer to the socket buffer containing the message.  
 * info (struct genl_info *): Pointer to the generic netlink information structure.  
 *  
 * Returns:  
 * int: Returns 0 on success, or a negative error code on failure.  
 *  
 * Logic:  
 * The function checks for the presence of device and target indices in the attributes.  
 * If either is missing, it returns an invalid argument error. It retrieves the device  
 * using the device index and deactivates the target using the target index. Finally,  
 * it releases the device reference and returns the result of the deactivation operation.  
 ******************************************************************************/
